sentence: Monday was the _____ day last week.
reason: Use a completed-week reference.

sentence: This is the _____ photo in our family album.
reason: Give the photo a clear comparison set.

sentence: Walking across at the zebra crossing is _____ crossing elsewhere on this road.
reason: Compare crossing choices rather than a crossing with a road.

sentence: The bus is _____ my car.
reason: Compare two similarly described objects.

sentence: Tom was _____ his brother before the game.
reason: Clarify the happiness comparison.

sentence: Ming was _____ Tom when they carried the glass cups.
reason: Clarify both boys' careful behaviour.

sentence: Of the students carrying glasses of water, Ming is the _____.
reason: Distinguish drinking glasses from spectacles.

sentence: This is the _____ idea for our school.
reason: Make the school reference clear.

sentence: The weather today is _____ yesterday’s.
reason: Compare weather, not worse rain.

sentence: This is _____ weather we have had this week.
reason: Clarify weather in the current week.

sentence: This has been _____ bus ride this week.
reason: Use a completed-experience reference.

sentence: The shop is _____ the school from my home.
reason: Clarify the shared distance reference.

sentence: From our home, the park is _____ the school.
reason: State the common distance reference first.

sentence: Of the four bowls, this one has the _____ rice.
reason: Make the bowl comparison set explicit.

sentence: Ming threw the ball _____ Tom did.
reason: Make the compared action explicit.

sentence: The bell rang _____ it did yesterday.
reason: Make the duration comparison explicit.

sentence: Of the teams, ours ran _____.
reason: Use a familiar clear action.

sentence: Tom studied _____ his brother did for the test.
reason: Clarify the effort comparison.

sentence: Tom studied _____ in his class.
reason: Use a natural comparison-group phrase.

sentence: The library opened _____ it did yesterday.
reason: Make the earlier-opening reference explicit.

sentence: The library opened _____ on Monday.
reason: Remove the awkward Of the days phrase.

sentence: Our lesson started _____ the lesson for the other class.
reason: Clarify that a lesson began, rather than a group.

sentence: In summer, the sun comes up _____ in winter.
reason: Use present tense for a general seasonal comparison.

sentence: Of my family, Dad gets up _____.
reason: Use a clearer familiar family routine.

sentence: Of all the teachers, Mr Lee spoke _____.
reason: Use a named speaker within a clear group.

sentence: Of the bus services, this one runs _____.
reason: Compare service frequency rather than single bus arrivals.

sentence: Of the students, Ming took the competition _____.
reason: Use the natural take seriously collocation.

sentence: Our team played _____ it did last time.
reason: Make the earlier action explicit.

sentence: Of all the teams, our team completed the challenge _____.
reason: Use a clearer action for successfully.

sentence: Of these clocks, this one is set _____.
reason: Use set correctly instead of show time correctly.

sentence: Of the cards, the blue one was _____ damaged by the rain.
reason: Use physical damage rather than marked badly.

sentence: Of all the students in my class, I worked _____.
reason: The retry found Among students too vague; use a clear class comparison set.
